note: Topical anti-TNF biologics (tanfanercept/HL036, licaminlimab/ESBA105) in unselected dry eye: desiccating-stress mouse and rabbit ocular-PK models; nothing approved, tanfanercept missed both Phase 3 co-primaries twice, licaminlimab is regrouping on a TNFR1 genotype.
label: Dry eye (anti-TNF)

engagement.note: Topical HL036 concentrated in cornea and anterior segment and eliminated ocular-surface TNF-α in desiccating-stress mice; no patient target-engagement readout has been published.
engagement.short: HL036 clears ocular-surface TNF-α in mice
engagement.quote: HL036 concentration was significantly higher in cornea and anterior segment than etanercept and effectively eliminated TNF-α on ocular surfaces.
engagement.judgement: The only patient-side target readout for this class (conjunctival TNFα/IL1β/IL8 mRNA and TNFR1-SNP response to licaminlimab, Donnenfeld et al., Cornea 2024, doi:10.1097/ICO.0000000000003510) was retracted in Oct 2024 (notice doi:10.1097/ICO.0000000000003640; reason not retrievable, PubMed/Europe PMC pages failed), so it cannot carry a status. Thiel 2013 measured ESBA105 in aqueous humor of cataract patients, which is exposure, not TNF-α neutralisation at the dry-eye target; it is used in the dose cell.

dose.note: Topical ESBA105 reached therapeutic concentrations in rabbit aqueous and vitreous with systemic exposure 25,000-fold below the same dose given i.v.
dose.short: Rabbit eye drops reach therapeutic levels
dose.quote: After topical administration to the eye, ESBA105 quickly reaches therapeutic concentrations in all ocular compartments.
dose.judgement: Epub 2008-08-29, print IOVS 2009; house convention takes 2009. Companion paper Ottiger 2009 (doi:10.1167/iovs.08-2372) mapped the corneal/scleral penetration routes in the same rabbit system.

dose.note: In cataract patients, topical ESBA105 reached aqueous-humor concentrations 96- to 359-fold above intraocular TNF-α, the therapeutic level the rabbit model predicted.
dose.quote: These results demonstrate that the topically applied single-chain antibody fragment ESBA105 penetrated into the anterior chamber of the human eye at therapeutic levels.
dose.reason: Human aqueous levels matched rabbit prediction
dose.judgement: Abstract only (Ophthalmology is paywalled; the Elsevier redirect could not be fetched), so whether the paper itself tabulates rabbit vs human concentrations is unverified; comparison_stated is therefore false and magnitude direction_only. Subjects were otherwise-healthy cataract-surgery patients (NCT00820014, no registry results posted), not dry-eye patients; the registry brief summary frames the study explicitly as testing the animal penetration finding in humans. A re-scorer who requires the comparison to be in the disease population should downgrade this to untested.

efficacy.note: Topical, not systemic, HL036 reduced corneal erosion and restored goblet cells in desiccating-stress C57BL/6 mice; dogs with spontaneous KCS later beat cyclosporine.
efficacy.quote: Corneal erosion and goblet cell counts were improved only with topically applied etanercept and HL036.
efficacy.judgement: A second, spontaneous-disease model was added in 2018 (naturally occurring canine KCS, Lee 2018, doi:10.1080/02713683.2018.1461909: HL036 more effective than 1% cyclosporine on clinical-sign scores and Schirmer); it does not change the status so it is not a separate strip entry.

efficacy.note: VELOS-2 (n=637) missed both co-primaries, inferior corneal staining p=0.187 and ocular discomfort p=0.555; VELOS-3 repeated the miss (p=0.764, p=0.144) in 2023.
efficacy.quote: Coprimary Endpoint: Change From Baseline in Inferior Corneal Fluorescein Staining Score to Day 57 (Pre- to Post-CAE) — 0.25% HL036 vs Placebo: 0.08 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.21), P-Value 0.1871
efficacy.reason: Mouse sign benefit; Phase 3 missed twice
efficacy.judgement: No peer-reviewed VELOS-2/VELOS-3 paper exists (PubMed and web search, 2026-11-02); the ClinicalTrials.gov results record is the primary source, as rule 1 allows, so the quote is assembled from the posted outcome title and statistical-analysis fields rather than a prose sentence. Status is contra rather than untested on the ad-amyloid precedent (trial result as source, comparison_stated false): the mouse readout is a corneal sign, and the sign co-primary failed in both pivotal trials. VELOS-3 (NCT05109702, results posted 2023-10-23): CCSS LS-mean difference -0.03 (95% CI -0.214 to 0.157), p=0.764; eye-dryness VAS 4.34 (-1.483 to 10.155), p=0.144. The premise of a 'Phase 2 signal' is weaker than billed: VELOS-1 (NCT03334539, results posted 2022-01-26) also missed its registered co-primaries (ICSS p=0.29/0.34, ODS p=0.15/0.23), and the China Phase 2 (Dong 2022, doi:10.1007/s10792-022-02245-1) reports its ICSS primary at p=0.65 under a positive title; the cited signal was the secondary central-staining score. The one Phase 2 primary hit in the class is licaminlimab on symptoms (Shettle 2022, doi:10.2147/OPTH.S366836, global ocular discomfort p=0.041, severe DED with persistent discomfort; registry primary AUC has no p-value posted), which the mouse model does not read out, so it neither confirms nor rescues the sign prediction. No source puts the mouse result beside the VELOS data. VELOS-4 (NCT06400589) is listed as suspended; Harbour's China Phase 3 (NCT04633213) completed 2022-08 with no posted results, not checked further.

safety.note: Rabbit topical PK predicted negligible systemic anti-TNF exposure; no GLP ocular toxicology for this class has been published.
safety.quote: Systemic exposure after topical administration is 25,000-fold lower than exposure after i.v. injection of the identical cumulative daily dose.
safety.judgement: What topical ocular tox predicted: nothing formal is in the literature. The published animal safety signals are this rabbit systemic-exposure result and 'No severe adverse reactions were noted' in the 2018 dog KCS study; tanfanercept's IND toxicology is unpublished.

safety.note: Severe-DED patients on licaminlimab: serum mostly undetectable (max 8.47 ng/mL), no IOP change, no safety issues; VELOS-2 serious AEs 5/318 vs 4/319, none ocular.
safety.quote: Topical ocular licaminlimab appears to be safe and well tolerated in this study, with no effect on IOP or other ophthalmic parameters, along with minimal systemic exposure.
safety.reason: Minimal systemic exposure held in patients
safety.judgement: Full text read (open access). Licaminlimab is ESBA105 renamed (Novartis then Oculis OCS-02), so product_in_model is true. The paper compares its serum levels with systemic anti-TNF agents, not with the rabbit data, hence comparison_stated false and magnitude direction_only. Trial is NCT01338610 (Alcon, 2011-12; results posted 2013-04-19; serious AEs 0 in all arms per registry), published a decade later. Corroboration from tanfanercept: VELOS-2 registry serious AEs 5/318 vs 4/319, all non-ocular; instillation-site pain 62/318 vs 58/319; Dong 2022 no serious AEs.
